The script detects your platform, verifies the release archive\nagainst the release's \u003ccode\u003echecksums.txt\u003c/code\u003e, and installs to \u003ccode\u003e/usr/local/bin\u003c/code\u003e (falling\nback to \u003ccode\u003e~/.local/bin\u003c/code\u003e) — reporting each step as it goes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"  [1/5] ✔ Detecting platform   darwin/arm64\n  [2/5] ✔ Resolving release    v0.2.2\n  [3/5] ⠹ Downloading release  ███████████░░░░░░░░░░░  52%  1.8M/3.5M\n  [4/5] ✔ Verifying checksum   sha256:cc309ae1c107\n  [5/5] ✔ Installing           /usr/local/bin/clawx\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003e  [1/5] ✔ Detecting platform   darwin/arm64\n  [2/5] ✔ Resolving release    v0.2.2\n  [3/5] ⠹ Downloading release  ███████████░░░░░░░░░░░  52%  1.8M/3.5M\n  [4/5] ✔ Verifying checksum   sha256:cc309ae1c107\n  [5/5] ✔ Installing           /usr/local/bin/clawx\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePin a version with \u003ccode\u003eCLAWX_VERSION=v0.2.2\u003c/code\u003e, change the destination with\n\u003ccode\u003eCLAWX_INSTALL_DIR\u003c/code\u003e, or set \u003ccode\u003eNO_COLOR=1\u003c/code\u003e for plain output (also the default when\nstdout is not a terminal, so CI logs stay clean). From a checkout,\n\u003ccode\u003emake install-latest\u003c/code\u003e runs the same script. See\n\u003ca href=\"#windows-powershell\"\u003eWindows\u003c/a\u003e and \u003ca href=\"#other-install-options\"\u003eother install options\u003c/a\u003e\nbelow.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eClawx shells out to an agent CLI, so you also need one of \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003eopencode\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egemini\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003eagy\u003c/code\u003e on your \u003ccode\u003ePATH\u003c/code\u003e. The default is \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e; select\nanother with \u003ccode\u003eCLAWX_PROVIDER\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003chr\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eReusable, versioned, checksummed tasks for coding agents — run with Claude Code,\nCodex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Antigravity. Search → inspect → approve →\nexecute, with a log of everything that ran.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ca target=\"_blank\" rel=\"noopener noreferrer\" href=\"/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/docs/demo.gif\"\u003e\u003cimg src=\"/debarshibasak/clawx/raw/master/docs/demo.gif\" alt=\"clawx demo: search, info, approval, execution, history\" data-animated-image=\"\" style=\"max-width: 100%;\"\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cem\u003eThe whole idea in 30 seconds: find a package, ask an agent what it would do,\nreview the approval prompt (checksum, parameters, tool grants), let your agent\nexecute it, and see the run land in your history. The output above is replayed\nfrom a real recorded session (\u003ca href=\"/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/docs/demo\"\u003edocs/demo/\u003c/a\u003e).\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA Clawx \u003cstrong\u003epackage\u003c/strong\u003e is a markdown file with YAML front matter. The front matter\ndeclares metadata — name, version, typed parameters, dependencies, the tools the\npackage wants. The body becomes the \u003cstrong\u003esystem prompt\u003c/strong\u003e of an agent CLI.\n\"Installing\" a package means: fetch it from a registry, verify its SHA256\nagainst the index, show an approval prompt, execute it under the agent you\nchose, and append the outcome to an execution log. There is no code generation\nand no compilation — the install \u003cem\u003eis\u003c/em\u003e a governed agent invocation.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-alert markdown-alert-warning\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cp class=\"markdown-alert-title\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-alert mr-2\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"M6.457 1.047c.659-1.234 2.427-1.234 3.086 0l6.082 11.378A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.082 15H1.918a1.75 1.75 0 0 1-1.543-2.575Zm1.763.707a.25.25 0 0 0-.44 0L1.698 13.132a.25.25 0 0 0 .22.368h12.164a.25.25 0 0 0 .22-.368Zm.53 3.996v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 11a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003eWarning\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecurity model — read this before running packages.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA package is a prompt executed by an agent with real tool access on your\nmachine. Treat running one with the same suspicion as \u003ccode\u003ecurl | sh\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eallowed_tools\u003c/code\u003e is enforced at the subprocess boundary only under the\n\u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e provider\u003c/strong\u003e, where it is forwarded as \u003ccode\u003e--allowedTools\u003c/code\u003e. Under\n\u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eopencode\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egemini\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eagy\u003c/code\u003e it is \u003cstrong\u003edisclosure in the approval\nprompt, not a Clawx-enforced boundary\u003c/strong\u003e — those CLIs govern tool access\nthrough their own sandboxing and approval modes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSHA256 verification proves the file you run is byte-identical to what the\nregistry indexed. It says nothing about whether those bytes are safe. A\nregistry is a trust root: only add registries you trust, and use\n\u003ccode\u003eclawx info\u003c/code\u003e to have a tool-less agent summarize a package before running it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eAgents are not deterministic and can misinterpret instructions. The\napproval prompt and the execution log exist to bound and audit that risk,\nnot to eliminate it.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy not shell scripts?\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-why-not-shell-scripts\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Why not shell scripts?\" href=\"#why-not-shell-scripts\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFair question — it's the first one everybody asks. A shell script encodes a\n\u003cem\u003emechanism\u003c/em\u003e: the exact commands that worked on the machines its author\nanticipated. A Clawx package encodes \u003cem\u003eintent\u003c/em\u003e — the goal, the constraints, the\nverification steps — and the agent picks the mechanism for the machine in front\nof it. The same \u003ccode\u003edockerize\u003c/code\u003e package containerizes a Go, Node, or Python repo\nbecause it detects the ecosystem instead of assuming it; a script would need a\ncase statement per ecosystem, per package manager, per layout, and it still\nbreaks on the repo its author never saw.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOn top of that, packages carry infrastructure scripts never accumulated:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTyped parameters\u003c/strong\u003e — declared in front matter with defaults; missing\nrequired ones are prompted for, not discovered as an unbound variable at\nruntime.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eDependencies\u003c/strong\u003e — \u003ccode\u003edepends_on\u003c/code\u003e resolves transitively against your\nregistries. A dependency whose \u003ccode\u003eprovides\u003c/code\u003e binaries are already on your PATH\ncounts as met; anything genuinely missing is listed for your approval before\nit is installed.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eProvider portability\u003c/strong\u003e — one package runs under \u003ccode\u003eclaude\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003ecodex\u003c/code\u003e,\n\u003ccode\u003eopencode\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003egemini\u003c/code\u003e, or \u003ccode\u003eagy\u003c/code\u003e; switching agents is an env var, not a rewrite.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA governed run\u003c/strong\u003e — SHA256 verification against the registry index, then an\napproval prompt listing the tools, env vars, and parameter values \u003cem\u003ebefore\u003c/em\u003e\nanything executes.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAn execution trail\u003c/strong\u003e — every run appends package, version, SHA, exit code,\nand duration to \u003ccode\u003e~/.clawx/execution.log\u003c/code\u003e. You can answer \"what ran on this\nmachine, when, and did it succeed?\"\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAnd the honest counterpoint: an agent run is slower than a script and not\ndeterministic — the same package produces a different transcript each time. If\nyour task is fully mechanical, keep the shell script (a package can simply call\nit). Clawx is for the judgment-shaped tasks where scripts rot: auditing,\nmigrating, configuring against whatever the repository actually contains.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eCandidly: if the task is deterministic, a script or Makefile is strictly\nbetter. If you manage fleets of machines toward a desired state, that's\nAnsible. Agent skills are the closest cousin — but they're tied to a single\nagent product and ship without versioned distribution, checksums, approval\ngates, or an execution log. Prompt libraries share text; nothing fetches,\nverifies, executes, or records it. Clawx occupies the gap: \u003cstrong\u003edistributable,\nverifiable, auditable tasks that need judgment at runtime.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eShowcase\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-showcase\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Showcase\" href=\"#showcase\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe packages that show what the model is for — multi-step, context-aware work,\nnot \u003ccode\u003ebrew install\u003c/code\u003e with extra steps:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e\u003ca href=\"/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/registry/packages/go-modernize.md\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ego-modernize\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e — audit an aging Go\nrepo: toolchain drift, deprecated APIs (\u003ccode\u003eioutil\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estrings.Title\u003c/code\u003e, ...), idiom\ndrift, outdated deps, vet/lint. <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debarshibasak/clawx/master/install.sh | sh"><pre>curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/debarshibasak/clawx/master/install.sh <span class="pl-k">|</span> sh</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">macOS and Linux. The script detects your platform, verifies the release archive
against the release's <code>checksums.txt</code>, and installs to <code>/usr/local/bin</code> (falling
back to <code>~/.local/bin</code>) — reporting each step as it goes:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="  [1/5] ✔ Detecting platform   darwin/arm64
  [2/5] ✔ Resolving release    v0.2.2
  [3/5] ⠹ Downloading release  ███████████░░░░░░░░░░░  52%  1.8M/3.5M
  [4/5] ✔ Verifying checksum   sha256:cc309ae1c107
  [5/5] ✔ Installing           /usr/local/bin/clawx"><pre class="notranslate"><code>  [1/5] ✔ Detecting platform   darwin/arm64
  [2/5] ✔ Resolving release    v0.2.2
  [3/5] ⠹ Downloading release  ███████████░░░░░░░░░░░  52%  1.8M/3.5M
  [4/5] ✔ Verifying checksum   sha256:cc309ae1c107
  [5/5] ✔ Installing           /usr/local/bin/clawx
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Pin a version with <code>CLAWX_VERSION=v0.2.2</code>, change the destination with
<code>CLAWX_INSTALL_DIR</code>, or set <code>NO_COLOR=1</code> for plain output (also the default when
stdout is not a terminal, so CI logs stay clean). From a checkout,
<code>make install-latest</code> runs the same script. See
<a href="#windows-powershell">Windows</a> and <a href="#other-install-options">other install options</a>
below.</p>
<p dir="auto">Clawx shells out to an agent CLI, so you also need one of <code>claude</code>, <code>codex</code>,
<code>opencode</code>, <code>gemini</code> or <code>agy</code> on your <code>PATH</code>. The default is <code>claude</code>; select
another with <code>CLAWX_PROVIDER</code>.</p>
<hr>
<p dir="auto">Reusable, versioned, checksummed tasks for coding agents — run with Claude Code,
Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, or Antigravity. Search → inspect → approve →
execute, with a log of everything that ran.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/docs/demo.gif"><img src="/debarshibasak/clawx/raw/master/docs/demo.gif" alt="clawx demo: search, info, approval, execution, history" data-animated-image="" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><em>The whole idea in 30 seconds: find a package, ask an agent what it would do,
review the approval prompt (checksum, parameters, tool grants), let your agent
execute it, and see the run land in your history. The output above is replayed
from a real recorded session (<a href="/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/docs/demo">docs/demo/</a>).</em></p>
<p dir="auto">A Clawx <strong>package</strong> is a markdown file with YAML front matter. The front matter
declares metadata — name, version, typed parameters, dependencies, the tools the
package wants. The body becomes the <strong>system prompt</strong> of an agent CLI.
"Installing" a package means: fetch it from a registry, verify its SHA256
against the index, show an approval prompt, execute it under the agent you
chose, and append the outcome to an execution log. There is no code generation
and no compilation — the install <em>is</em> a governed agent invocation.</p>
<div class="markdown-alert markdown-alert-warning" dir="auto"><p class="markdown-alert-title" dir="auto"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-alert mr-2" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M6.457 1.047c.659-1.234 2.427-1.234 3.086 0l6.082 11.378A1.75 1.75 0 0 1 14.082 15H1.918a1.75 1.75 0 0 1-1.543-2.575Zm1.763.707a.25.25 0 0 0-.44 0L1.698 13.132a.25.25 0 0 0 .22.368h12.164a.25.25 0 0 0 .22-.368Zm.53 3.996v2.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.5 0v-2.5a.75.75 0 0 1 1.5 0ZM9 11a1 1 0 1 1-2 0 1 1 0 0 1 2 0Z"></path></svg>Warning</p><p dir="auto"><strong>Security model — read this before running packages.</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">A package is a prompt executed by an agent with real tool access on your
machine. Treat running one with the same suspicion as <code>curl | sh</code>.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><code>allowed_tools</code> is enforced at the subprocess boundary only under the
<code>claude</code> provider</strong>, where it is forwarded as <code>--allowedTools</code>. Under
<code>codex</code>, <code>opencode</code>, <code>gemini</code>, and <code>agy</code> it is <strong>disclosure in the approval
prompt, not a Clawx-enforced boundary</strong> — those CLIs govern tool access
through their own sandboxing and approval modes.</li>
<li>SHA256 verification proves the file you run is byte-identical to what the
registry indexed. It says nothing about whether those bytes are safe. A
registry is a trust root: only add registries you trust, and use
<code>clawx info</code> to have a tool-less agent summarize a package before running it.</li>
<li>Agents are not deterministic and can misinterpret instructions. The
approval prompt and the execution log exist to bound and audit that risk,
not to eliminate it.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Why not shell scripts?</h2><a id="user-content-why-not-shell-scripts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Why not shell scripts?" href="#why-not-shell-scripts"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Fair question — it's the first one everybody asks. A shell script encodes a
<em>mechanism</em>: the exact commands that worked on the machines its author
anticipated. A Clawx package encodes <em>intent</em> — the goal, the constraints, the
verification steps — and the agent picks the mechanism for the machine in front
of it. The same <code>dockerize</code> package containerizes a Go, Node, or Python repo
because it detects the ecosystem instead of assuming it; a script would need a
case statement per ecosystem, per package manager, per layout, and it still
breaks on the repo its author never saw.</p>
<p dir="auto">On top of that, packages carry infrastructure scripts never accumulated:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Typed parameters</strong> — declared in front matter with defaults; missing
required ones are prompted for, not discovered as an unbound variable at
runtime.</li>
<li><strong>Dependencies</strong> — <code>depends_on</code> resolves transitively against your
registries. A dependency whose <code>provides</code> binaries are already on your PATH
counts as met; anything genuinely missing is listed for your approval before
it is installed.</li>
<li><strong>Provider portability</strong> — one package runs under <code>claude</code>, <code>codex</code>,
<code>opencode</code>, <code>gemini</code>, or <code>agy</code>; switching agents is an env var, not a rewrite.</li>
<li><strong>A governed run</strong> — SHA256 verification against the registry index, then an
approval prompt listing the tools, env vars, and parameter values <em>before</em>
anything executes.</li>
<li><strong>An execution trail</strong> — every run appends package, version, SHA, exit code,
and duration to <code>~/.clawx/execution.log</code>. You can answer "what ran on this
machine, when, and did it succeed?"</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">And the honest counterpoint: an agent run is slower than a script and not
deterministic — the same package produces a different transcript each time. If
your task is fully mechanical, keep the shell script (a package can simply call
it). Clawx is for the judgment-shaped tasks where scripts rot: auditing,
migrating, configuring against whatever the repository actually contains.</p>

<p dir="auto">Candidly: if the task is deterministic, a script or Makefile is strictly
better. If you manage fleets of machines toward a desired state, that's
Ansible. Agent skills are the closest cousin — but they're tied to a single
agent product and ship without versioned distribution, checksums, approval
gates, or an execution log. Prompt libraries share text; nothing fetches,
verifies, executes, or records it. Clawx occupies the gap: <strong>distributable,
verifiable, auditable tasks that need judgment at runtime.</strong></p>

<p dir="auto">The packages that show what the model is for — multi-step, context-aware work,
not <code>brew install</code> with extra steps:</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong><a href="/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/registry/packages/go-modernize.md"><code>go-modernize</code></a></strong> — audit an aging Go
repo: toolchain drift, deprecated APIs (<code>ioutil</code>, <code>strings.Title</code>, ...), idiom
drift, outdated deps, vet/lint. Writes a risk-grouped <code>MODERNIZE.md</code>;
with <code>-p apply=true</code> it applies the mechanical fixes and proves build and tests
stay green (it refuses to touch a dirty working tree, and reverts anything that
breaks). This is the package in the demo above.</p>

<p dir="auto">The Windows archive is named <code>clawx_<tag>_windows_amd64.tar.gz</code>. In
PowerShell, download it with the matching <code>checksums.txt</code>, verify the SHA256,
and put <code>clawx.exe</code> in a directory on your user <code>PATH</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-powershell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$tag = "v0.2.1" # replace with the release tag you downloaded
$archive = "clawx_${tag}_windows_amd64.tar.gz"
$base = "https://github.com/debarshibasak/clawx/releases/download/$tag"

Invoke-WebRequest "$base/$archive" -OutFile ".\$archive"
Invoke-WebRequest "$base/checksums.txt" -OutFile .\checksums.txt
$expected = Get-Content .\checksums.txt |
  Where-Object { $_ -match "\s$([regex]::Escape($archive))$" } |
  ForEach-Object { ($_ -split "\s+")[0] } |
  Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $expected) { throw "No checksum found for $archive" }
$actual = (Get-FileHash ".\$archive" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($actual -ne $expected.ToLowerInvariant()) { throw "SHA256 verification failed" }

tar -xzf ".\$archive"
$installDir = Join-Path $env:USERPROFILE "bin"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $installDir | Out-Null
Move-Item -Force .\clawx.exe (Join-Path $installDir "clawx.exe")
$userPath = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path", "User")
$pathEntries = @($userPath -split ";" | Where-Object { $_ })
if ($pathEntries -notcontains $installDir) {
  [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", (($pathEntries + $installDir) -join ";"), "User")
}
$env:Path = "$installDir;$env:Path"

<p dir="auto">PowerShell stores Clawx state under <code>%USERPROFILE%\.clawx</code> (the equivalent of
<code>~/.clawx</code> on macOS/Linux). <code>clawx list</code> uses <code>$env:PAGER</code> when stdout is a
terminal and falls back to <code>more</code>; use <code>clawx list --no-pager</code> or set
<code>$env:CLAWX_NO_PAGER = "1"</code> for non-interactive output.</p>
<p dir="auto">WSL is a separate environment: a Linux Clawx binary uses the Linux home
directory (<code>~/.clawx</code>) and Linux provider CLIs. A Windows binary launched from
PowerShell uses <code>%USERPROFILE%\.clawx</code> and needs the selected provider CLI on
the Windows <code>PATH</code>; the two environments do not share state automatically.</p>

<p dir="auto">Already have clawx? It updates itself the way it runs everything else — the
built-in registry ships an <code>install-clawx</code> package that fetches the latest
release, verifies its checksum, and installs the binary:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="clawx run install-clawx"><pre>clawx run install-clawx</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Like every run, it goes through the approval prompt first, and the execution is
logged to <code>~/.clawx/execution.log</code>.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto"><code>clawx rolladice</code></h3><a id="user-content-clawx-rolladice" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: clawx rolladice" href="#clawx-rolladice"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Rolls the dice on what to install next. It scans the current directory for
<strong>projects</strong> (ecosystem manifests), <strong>libraries</strong> (parsed out of those
manifests), <strong>containers</strong> (Dockerfile, compose, Kubernetes, Helm,
devcontainer) and <strong>notable files</strong> (CI, IaC, build, test, lint, data, docs) —
then matches all of that against the catalogs served by your registries.</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="  Detected:
    [*] go                 go.mod (github.com/acme/svc)
    [*] dockerfile         Dockerfile
    [*] kubernetes         deploy/app.yaml
    [*] ci:github-actions  .github/workflows/ci.yml

  Roll:

    1. base-setup               v1.0.0     score 72
       Prepare a Go service repository with linting and CI
       - required by installed analytics
       - matches your workspace: go, ci
       clawx run base-setup"><pre class="notranslate"><code>  Detected:
    [*] go                 go.mod (github.com/acme/svc)
    [*] dockerfile         Dockerfile
    [*] kubernetes         deploy/app.yaml
    [*] ci:github-actions  .github/workflows/ci.yml

  Roll:

    1. base-setup               v1.0.0     score 72
       Prepare a Go service repository with linting and CI
       - required by installed analytics
       - matches your workspace: go, ci
       clawx run base-setup
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Ranking is deterministic and runs offline: unmet dependencies of installed
packages outrank packages that build on installed ones, which outrank
workspace-signal and shared-vocabulary matches. The shortlist is then handed to
the agent, which explains the picks — a read-only call with no tools granted.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><code>--fast</code> skips both the workspace walk <em>and</em> the agent, ranking purely from
what you already have installed. It returns in milliseconds.</li>
<li><code>--no-agent</code> prints the offline shortlist without invoking any agent.</li>
</ul>
<p dir="auto">Only manifest files are ever opened. <code>.env</code> files and your source files are
recorded by path and never read.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Package format</h2><a id="user-content-package-format" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Package format" href="#package-format"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto"><code>depends_on</code> packages are resolved transitively before the package runs. A
dependency is considered satisfied if clawx has installed it before, or if every
executable it declares under <code>provides</code> is already on your PATH — so a machine
that already has Docker is never asked to install it. Whatever is left is shown
as a tree and installed only after you approve:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="This package requires 1 dependency that is not on this system:
    └─ install-docker (not found)

Install 1 missing dependency? [y/N]:"><pre class="notranslate"><code>This package requires 1 dependency that is not on this system:
    └─ install-docker (not found)

Install 1 missing dependency? [y/N]:
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">An <code>install-*</code> package declares what it puts on PATH:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="name: install-gh-cli
provides:
  - gh"><pre><span class="pl-ent">name</span>: <span class="pl-s">install-gh-cli</span>
<span class="pl-ent">provides</span>:
  - <span class="pl-s">gh</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Omit <code>provides</code> when there is no PATH binary to look for — a GUI app or a shell
function — and clawx falls back to its own installation records.
Fixtures live in <a href="/debarshibasak/clawx/blob/master/testdata/packages">testdata/packages/</a>.</p>
